transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I just seem to worry about everything lately. I mean, everything. My clients, the real estate market, my family, money... even little things, like whether moving into my new condo was the right decision. It just feels like it's out of proportion to what's actually going on, you know? It's just constant.
Did your worrying start after a specific stressful event?

Well, I suppose it did start around a specific time. This has been going on for about a year and two months now. That's when I sold the house I'd lived in for a long time and moved into the condo. The worrying really seemed to pick up after that.
When the worrying starts, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yes, it's very hard. Even when I try to stop and tell myself, Parin, this is not urgent... it doesn't really work. One concern just leads right to another. And before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour replaying small details that I really meant to let go.
For most of the past 6 months, have you been worrying like this more days than not?
Yes, definitely. Um, it's pretty much every day, to be honest. So it has certainly been more days than not for the past six months.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

No, I haven't really noticed feeling restless. Um, I don't feel on edge in a physical way, if that makes sense. I can sit still at my desk or on the couch just fine. It's really just the thoughts in my head that keep going, but I don't have that jumpy feeling.
Because of the worrying, do you have trouble concentrating?

Yes, I do. Um, especially at work. When I’m reviewing purchase agreements or inspection addendums, I’ll find myself reading the same paragraph three or four times. A worry just pops in, and I completely lose the thread of what I was checking.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
No, I wouldn't say that. Um, I don't really feel depressed or sad. My mood is generally fine, to be honest. It's really just the constant worrying about things that gets to me, but I don't feel down.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking things, like locks, paperwork, or other details, because you feel you have to?

No, I don't do that. I mean, I obviously check my real estate contracts to make sure they're correct, but it's not like an urge where I feel forced to keep checking them over and over. And I don't have any issues with checking locks or the stove or anything like that at home. Once I lock the door, I know it's done.
Do you feel that most of your worrying is mainly about the move to the condo and its consequences?

Well, no, I wouldn't say it's mainly about that. I mean, the condo move is definitely something I think about, but I worry about a lot of other things, too. Work, my clients, just... everyday life stuff. It really feels like there's always something I'm stressing over, so it's definitely not just limited to the move.
